title: Satisfactory safety and immunogenicity of MSP3 malaria vaccine candidate in Tanzanian children aged 12-24 months.
ehr_evidence: Participant information was captured on paper case report forms (CRFs), which were double-entered into a Microsoft Access data base.
summary: Phase Ib dose-escalation trial evaluating the safety and immunogenicity of the MSP3 malaria vaccine candidate in Tanzanian children aged 12–24 months.
key_findings: Grade 3 adverse events were infrequent, with only five detected throughout the study, all transient and resolved without sequelae.
Both 15 μg and 30 μg MSP3 dose regimens elicited strong cytophilic IgG1 and IgG3 antibody responses.
At day 84, 100% (15/15) and 83.3% (10/12) of children in the 15 μg and 30 μg MSP3 groups, respectively, showed an 8-fold increase in IgG1 antibodies.
All infants in the comparative analysis seroconverted with a mean titre of 10.68 ± 4.64 AU.
captured_features: solicited local and systemic adverse events
anti-MSP3 antibody titres (IgG, IgG1, IgG3, IgG2, IgG4, IgM)
study_design: randomized, double-blind, dose-escalation phase Ib clinical trial
population: children aged 12–24 months in Korogwe, Tanzania
limitations: subcutaneous administration route for MSP3 versus intramuscular for control may confound reactogenicity comparison
no efficacy or protective outcome data collected
